title: Legal text classification in Korean sexual offense cases: from traditional machine learning to large language models with XAI insights
abstract: arXiv:2610.00087v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The advancement of natural language processing (NLP) has expanded AI-based text classification in the legal domain. However, accurately classifying legal documents remains challenging due to the complexity of legal texts and subtle differences between legal categories. This study evaluates legal text classification models ranging from traditional machine learning techniques to large language models (LLMs) using ten categories of Korean sexual offense precedents. The results show that fine-tuning small-scale models such as KLUE-BERT on legal data outperforms general-purpose models such as GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.0, as well as traditional machine learning models. KLUE-BERT achieved the highest accuracy of 99.3%, indicating that domain adaptation and fine-tuning can be more important than model size for legal document classification. We further employ explainable AI (XAI) techniques to analyze model predictions and misclassification cases. XAI

translated_title: 韩国性犯罪案件中的法律文本分类：从传统机器学习到结合可解释AI洞察的大语言模型
translated_abstract: 自然语言处理（NLP）的进步扩展了基于AI的文本分类在法律领域的应用。然而，由于法律文本的复杂性以及法律类别之间的细微差异，准确分类法律文档仍然具有挑战性。本研究使用十类韩国性犯罪判例，评估了从传统机器学习技术到大语言模型（LLMs）的法律文本分类模型。结果表明，在法律数据上微调的小规模模型（如KLUE-BERT）的表现优于GPT-3.5和GPT-4.0等通用模型以及传统机器学习模型。KLUE-BERT达到了99.3%的最高准确率，表明对于法律文档分类而言，领域适应和微调可能比模型规模更为重要。我们进一步采用可解释AI（XAI）技术来分析模型预测和误分类案例。XAI
tldr: 本研究通过韩国性犯罪判例分类实验发现，在法律数据上微调的小规模模型KLUE-BERT准确率达99.3%，超越GPT-3.5、GPT-4.0等大语言模型和传统机器学习方法，证明领域适应与微调比模型规模更重要，并利用可解释AI技术深入分析模型预测与误分类原因。
en_tdlr: Fine-tuned small-scale models like KLUE-BERT achieve 99.3% accuracy on Korean sexual offense legal text classification, outperforming GPT-3.5, GPT-4.0, and traditional machine learning methods, demonstrating that domain adaptation and fine-tuning matter more than model size, with XAI providing insights into predictions and misclassifications.
